sources.title: team conversion of the frost limit to NASA POWER frost days
sources.locator: The sources give frost damage at about -1 to -2 °C for a couple of hours (FAO-66 potato: 1 °C and less). NASA POWER FROST_DAYS counts any day with frost at or below 0 °C, so one frost day does not show damaging cold. Threshold 1 means more than one, i.e. two or more frost days in the month (the engine counts FROST_DAYS > threshold). This conversion is ours, not the sources'.

sources.title: Bueckert, Pea yield formation in warming temperatures: phenological mechanisms (University of Saskatchewan research project page, published by Saskatchewan Pulse Growers, a producer group)
sources.locator: "Project Description": "A few days of heat above 29°C in the field causes flower and young pod abortion and lowers yield." Heat row: June (flowering and pod set), threshold 29 °C on NASA POWER daily T2M_MAX; since D43 (#113) a month counts as a heat month only with at least hazards.heat.minDays = 3 days above the threshold, which matches "a few days". At the Poznań field 6 of 45 Junes (1981-2025) have 3 or more such days (1996, 2000, 2016, 2019, 2021, 2022; NASA POWER daily, excerpt data/samples/power/daily-t2mmax-june-1981-2025-poznan.json).
